card.summary: Open-source CLI - Free tunnels - 3 free apps. The 3-second tunnel that started it all - still free, still first-class. HTTPS, WebSocket, TCP, UDP, TLS.

free_tier.stated: Open-source CLI - Free tunnels - 3 free apps. The 3-second tunnel that started it all - still free, still first-class. HTTPS, WebSocket, TCP, UDP, TLS.

egress.terms: No byte allowance is published. The deploy path caps the compressed upload at 50 MB, which is a deploy limit and not a tunnel allowance.; ingress: http-only

record.interface_detail: tunr share --port 3000, tunr deploy, and an MCP tool surface.
record.tooling: brew install ahmetvural79/tap/tunr, or go install; an MCP server exposes tunr_deploy.
record.chaining: Replaces a free VM for static demos; cannot carry a WireGuard handshake or a raw game protocol.

limits.value: UDP never reaches the wire: raw TCP and UDP are only framed onto a WebSocket, so a WireGuard client cannot dial it at all. That gate binds before any allowance.
compressed deploy upload limited to 50 MB

record.binding_note: UDP never reaches the wire: raw TCP and UDP are only framed onto a WebSocket, so a WireGuard client cannot dial it at all. That gate binds before any allowance.

identity_cost.detail: Deploying an app needs a dashboard account at app.tunr.sh; share tunnels appear usable from the CLI. The signup form was not read.

record.reliability_note: Deployed apps sleep when idle and wake in about 150 ms; the tunnel tier is a marketing on-ramp to the deploy product, so it can be repriced.
record.confidence_note: A probe against a live tunnel would confirm the WebSocket-only framing; the docs state it plainly.

evidence.proved: Free tunnels, 3 free apps, and the claim of HTTPS, WebSocket, TCP, UDP and TLS support.
TCP, UDP and TLS are experimental and exposed only as a WebSocket stream; there is no raw TCP/UDP port on the relay yet.

record.notes: Launched 2026-06-21 as a 3-second tunnel and has since pivoted to an app-deploy platform. The homepage claim of TCP and UDP support is true only in the WebSocket-framing sense, which the docs admit.

extras.wg_detail: The relay has no raw UDP port yet: the docs say the relay exposes a raw tunnel only as a WebSocket stream at wss://<subdomain>.tunr.sh/tunnel/tcp (binary frames carry the bytes). There's no raw TCP/UDP port on the relay yet, so native clients like psql or ssh can't connect directly.
extras.volume_stated: No byte allowance is published. The deploy path caps the compressed upload at 50 MB, which is a deploy limit and not a tunnel allowance.
extras.transit_note: The tunr.sh edge relay carries the bytes over WebSocket.
